messages.text: I'm looking for a globe for a 12 year old that will be suitable now and in the future.

For a 12-year-old who'll keep using it for years, I'd steer away from the younger-kid interactive globes and toward something that grows with them: the Replogle Intelliglobe II 12" Interactive Desk Globe with Wireless Pen. It pairs a real raised-relief political map with an AR/interactive learning layer, so it works for school projects now but still looks and functions like a proper adult desk globe later on, not something they'll outgrow.

Is this mainly for homework and school use, or more for their room as something to explore on their own?
for exploring.  I don't want one with technology that could become obsolete

That makes sense — no batteries or pens to worry about down the road. For pure hands-on exploring, the Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe with its Gyromatic base is a great fit: no electronics at all, just a well-built globe with raised-relief mountains you can actually feel and trace, so it's engaging for a curious 12-year-old now and still a serious, good-looking globe on their desk as an adult.

You'll find it under "Eureka 16" Blue Ocean Raised Relief Globe" in the search bar, ready to add to your cart.
